notes: InterruptOnConfig (the config shape passed to HumanInTheLoopMiddleware) has exactly four fields - allowed_decisions, description, args_schema, when - none of which express 'approve this tool/argument-pattern for all future calls'. `when` is a per-call predicate the application can write statefully (e.g. closing over a set of already-approved args) to APPROXIMATE standing approval, but that is an application-built pattern, not a framework primitive comparable to openai-agents' always_approve or agent-framework's ToolApprovalRule. Raw langgraph.types.interrupt() has no approval concept at all - it is a generic pause/resume primitive. H3 is therefore NOT_APPLICABLE at the langgraph/langchain layer as tested, distinct from a PASS (property held) or a FAIL (property violated) - there is no standing-approval surface here to characterize the scope of.

state_boundary.note: no runtime execution - this is a static source-introspection check
